chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn from Zur'ah from Sama'ah said:

I asked him about a man who sold a female slave on the condition that she was a virgin, but he did not find her to be so. He said: 'She is not returned to him, nor is anything obligatory upon him, because she may have lost her virginity due to an illness or an ailment that affected her.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a bought slave girl is not found to have the promised attribute of virginity?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the sale of a female slave is not voided if the attribute of virginity is found to be missing, as the defect may have occurred naturally after the transaction due to illness or other factors. This ruling emphasizes the principle of *gharar* (uncertainty) being minimal in such cases, distinguishing it from deliberate fraud, and reflects the Shia juristic view that the buyer bears the risk of natural changes post-sale unless otherwise specified. The hadith underscores the importance of contextualizing defects in sales contracts within the framework of customary practice and natural occurrence.
